$comment: Copy to <your-repo>/night-agent.config.json and edit briefs to fit the project. Missions rotate by neglect; models rotate per harness; each harness runs in its own reset-anchored spend window. Machine-wide defaults may also live in ~/.config/night-agent/config.json (repo file wins; missions come only from the repo file).

missions.name: deps
missions.brief: Review outdated or vulnerable dependencies. Apply patch and minor updates that satisfy the safe-change policy, with release notes reviewed, lockfiles updated, and focused tests run. Record major upgrades as decision items instead of applying them.

missions.name: compat
missions.brief: Keep this project compatible with the current state of the protocols and critical libraries it depends on. Read-only network access is authorized for this mission. First infer, from manifests, lockfiles, imports, and NIGHT_AGENT.md, which external protocols the project implements and which dependencies are load-bearing (cryptography, consensus, networking, auth, serialization, data formats). For each, look for upstream releases, security advisories, deprecations, and protocol changes since the last check. Classify every finding: a change mandated by an authoritative source — a published security advisory (CVE, GHSA, or a vendor emergency notice) applying to a version this project uses, or a required protocol transition that would otherwise break interoperability — is REQUIRED work; apply it and the code changes needed to restore the build and tests even when it forces a major or code-incompatible dependency upgrade, and record the advisory reference and your migration reasoning. A merely newer version, an optional feature, or a backward-incompatible change with no authoritative mandate goes to Needs Your Decision with evidence, impact, and a recommendation — never apply it speculatively. Never weaken security or tests to make things compile; if a mandatory upgrade cannot be completed safely and verifiably this run, leave the worktree clean and record the precise blocker. Never push.

missions.name: upstream
missions.brief: This repository is a fork. Read-only network fetch of the configured upstream is authorized for this mission. Review upstream commits since the last merge point, summarize relevant changes as findings, and cherry-pick or merge only clean, conflict-free, behavior-compatible commits. Anything with conflicts or API changes goes to Needs Your Decision. Never push.
